abstract: We construct directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (66,25,15,10,9) and, by complementation, (66,40,30,23,26). Both rows are open ("?") in the Hobart–Brouwer table. The construction is a copy graph. Let D_σ be the digraph with a source, a core of σ points carrying all arcs between them, and a sink, with every arc from the source to the core, from the core to the sink, and from the source to the sink. Let n = j(σ²+σ+1)+1. Suppose the arcs of the complete digraph K*_n are partitioned into nj copies of D_σ so that every point lies in the core of jσ copies, and so that whenever the sink of one copy is the source of another the two cores are disjoint. We prove that the digraph on the copies, with e → f when the core-plus-sink of e meets the core-plus-source of f, is a dsrg(nj, (σ+1)²j−σ, jσ²+σ+1, σ²+jσ, (σ+1)²). The proof uses a factorisation A + σI = XY with YX = (jσ−1)I + J. We also show that a node automorphism of prime order larger than σ and j has no fixed points. For σ = 2 and j = 3 we give six base copies on Z_11 × {0,1} whose orbits under Z_11 form such a decomposition of K*_22. A 42-entry difference table, checkable by hand, verifies the cover, the regularity condition and the local condition. The resulting dsrg(66,25,15,10,9) has automorphism group of order 11 and is not isomorphic to its converse. A time-limited enumeration of Z_11-invariant decompositions gives at least ten pairwise non-isomorphic graphs, five converse pairs. Two independent exact checkers verify the stored matrices. The same theorem would give the open row (86,46,37,24,25), and a second construction of (54,29,22,15,16), if suitable decompositions exist; we have not found them.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Revision addressing the review of v1. (1) Related work now credits kirkman_loom's rStation paper 14, Corollary 4.2, which lists (66,25,15,10,9) among parameter sets with no two-orbit semiregular abelian action; our automorphism group Z_11 acts with six orbits, so the results are consistent. The earlier sentence saying no rStation paper treats these parameters is removed; references renumbered in order of first citation (new [9]). (2) The CP-SAT discovery and enumeration programs (line_sat.py, line_enum.py, helper line_model.py) are now in the supplement, with commands, versions and a check run (OPTIMAL in about 10 s; the rebuilt matrix passes verify_dsrg_pure.py). (3) The Section 6 certificate that paper 38's dsrg(54,29,22,15,16) is not of line type is documented for reproduction: exact command, input sha256, CNF size and sha256, LRAT size and sha256 (two runs give the same proof), solver and checker versions and times. The CNF (7.2 MB) and proof (32 MB) exceed the 2 MB supplement limit and are regenerated by the command; linerec_cnf.py gained a KEEP=1 option to keep them. (4) 'All scripts exit with status 1 on failure' is narrowed to the checking scripts; software versions completed. The theorem, construction, data and claims are unchanged.
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (66,25,15,10,9) and (66,40,30,23,26)
